text:
alex: Heads-up — canary shows quota attribution spike after we rolled the route-header shim in py/ts clients. Console is reporting ~30% higher burn for a subset of tenants.

maria: Which shim exactly? the move to `x-rd-route` on the wire?

alex: Yup. Repro steps: 1) send request with legacy header `Route-ID: my-tenant` 2) client shim converts to `x-rd-route: {id,priority}` 3) console groups appear to treat the hashed x-rd-route as a different key.

jamal: I saw that in canary logs too. meter-proxy preserves `route_key=my-tenant` but ingest pipeline shows `route_key=hash:abcd1234`. Ingest canonicalizer is hashing x-rd-route.

nora: That would cause double-counting in the console dashboard vs quota ledger if they index differently. We changed canonical IDs earlier this cycle.

infra-bot: deploy/ingest-service v2.14 -> canary triggered by @alex at 2026-03-22T18:02:11Z :rocket:

maria: Can someone paste a curl that reproduces so I can run a quick check?

alex: `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Route-ID: tenant-42" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"test"}'` — client shim (py/ts) will rewrite to `x-rd-route`.

jamal: Run that against canary and compare meter-proxy vs ingest logs. I can see the mismatch locally: meter-proxy route_key=tenant-42, ingest route_key=hash:abcd1234.

maria: We need a short mitigation. Options: (A) make ingest emit unhashed route key, (B) teach quota ledger to accept hashed keys and map, (C) do console-side merge during canary window.

nora: (C) is lowest-risk for canary. Add reconciliation/mapping layer in console and a UI toggle to merge hashed/unhashed counts.

alex: I'll export observed (Route-ID -> hash) CSV from canary logs and drop it in #eng-runtime.

jamal: Note: we shipped the shim default-on in the last minor release for Python and TS. I'm happy to flip it to opt-in until backend aligns.

nora: Please do. Feature-flag the shim across languages and stop default enable until ingestion and meter-proxy agree on canonicalization.

console: I'll add a reconciliation job and dashboard panel showing hashed vs unhashed key traffic. Will also add an annotation on tenant pages warning about potential canary attribution artifacts.

alex: Action list: 1) @jamal cut patch to revert py/ts default -> opt-in (branch: fix/shim-opt-in) 2) @maria build temporary console mapping + dashboard 3) @nora sync ingest and meter-proxy canonicalizer behavior 4) alex will upload mapping csv. Aim: freeze defaults in 24h, reconciliation live in 48h.

maria: I'll scope the console work and spin up a canary dashboard tile.

jamal: Opening PR now: https://github.com/redwood-inference/clients/pull/1234 — branch `fix/shim-opt-in`.

nora: Once PR is up I'll run an end-to-end test. If green we can gate re-enable behind a metric: divergence <5% for a rolling 24h window.

alex: Keep language to tenants conservative; mark any tenant-facing note as "internal canary artifact" until reconciled. :white_check_mark:

maria: Also logging idea: emit a telemetry event when shim rewrites header so we can correlate on the ingest side. Low-cost and helps mapping.

jamal: Good call. I'll add an opt-in telemetry toggle in the SDKs so we can ship the event without exposing it by default.

nora: Thanks everyone. Let's reconvene after the PR and initial reconciliation run.

alex: 👍
